title: Choose the visual world for the tech-prep desktop app
question: The roll assigned the Dojo Name Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Three more catalog worlds wait in the re-roll pool (convention catalog grid, Crouwel grid specimen, variable-font specimen).

options.label: Dojo Name Board
options.lineage: the nafudakake: wooden name plates hung on a dojo wall in order of rank
options.thesis: Every concept is a wooden name plate that climbs the wall as you earn it.
options.viewport: Indigo rail and tutor pane frame a dark Neovim pane; the problem's concept plates hang face-down above it until the review ends.
options.risk: Can slide into Japanese kitsch if brush fonts or ornaments creep in; plates must stay small and functional.

raised.raise: Tutor prose is held to a fixed 60-character measure; extra width becomes margin, never longer lines.
Today's session strip always shows what remains, and finished tasks stay visible as done.

options.label: Field Guide Plates
options.lineage: Peterson field guides: field marks arrowed on facing plates
options.thesis: Recognition is the skill, so every problem shows its field marks: the cues that identify the pattern.
options.viewport: Light page with an olive rail; after the review, thin pointer lines tie cue phrases in the statement to the concept they reveal.
options.risk: A light shell can clash with a dark Neovim theme, and plates can read as a book instead of a working screen.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.lineage: the Metro design language: flat tiles and giant lowercase type
options.thesis: Type is the interface: giant lowercase headings and flat colour tiles, with no chrome.
options.viewport: Black ground, a cropped giant 'today' heading, session tasks as flat tiles, tutor prose in large type beside the editor.
options.case: Fuses well: big type and flat state colours read at a glance; loses on audience fit because it reads as 2012 Windows.
options.risk: Giant type eats space a coding screen needs, and the association is dated.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder and Plate
options.lineage: nineteenth-century lexicon pages with colour plates
options.thesis: Black text to a fixed measure, guide words naming the span in view, colour only inside plates.
options.viewport: A roadmap set as lexicon columns with guide words at the head.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a coding learner does not identify with a dictionary, and quarantined colour fights state colours.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a tool.
options.kept: Its measure discipline: prose never runs past 60 characters.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: 1960s airline ticket wallets with carbon coupons
options.thesis: A session as a coupon book: each task tears off and the wallet shows what remains.
options.viewport: Today's tasks as coupons, the current one open.
options.case: Fuses poorly: VOID stamps clash with a product that has no failure state, and travel has nothing to do with learning.
options.risk: Costume of paper ephemera on a working screen.
options.kept: Its sequence discipline: the session always shows what remains.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: LeetCode's three-column dark IDE, executed cleanly: statement, editor, chat.
canonCard.viewport: Problem tabs left, Neovim centre, tutor chat right, test console under the editor.
